candidate_relations.reason: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is a different genetic platelet disorder and does not explain the saturation-linked platelet swings.
Ebstein anomaly is a different congenital heart lesion from the documented pulmonary atresia with VSD.
Anemia is a different hematologic finding; hematocrit rose with cyanosis rather than defining the platelet diagnosis.
Tricuspid atresia is not the echocardiographic diagnosis in this newborn.
Postoperative thrombocytosis asserts the opposite platelet direction from the hypoxia-linked thrombocytopenia.
Jacobsen syndrome is a different genetic thrombocytopenia and is not supported by the record.
Pulmonary atresia with VSD is the cardiac source of hypoxia but is not the platelet diagnosis itself.
Ventricular septal defect is an associated cardiac finding, not hypoxia-induced thrombocytopenia.
Pulmonary atresia is the associated cardiac lesion producing cyanosis, not the thrombocytopenia diagnosis.
Glanzmann thrombasthenia is a qualitative platelet disorder, not count suppression tied to hypoxia.
Congenital heart disease with TAR syndrome asserts an incompatible genetic thrombocytopenia rather than reversible hypoxia-related counts.

case_quality_flags: No complete_equivalent candidate; hypoxia-induced thrombocytopenia is not named in the registry
